contexts.text: Such persons are described in the Word... when their good is not as yet so much defiled; then, when it is defiled; and afterwards, when it is altogether defiled. AC 2468:3. AC 2468:6. AC 2468:10. AC 4174.
Under Most Ancient Church, see this reference.
They had been endowed with a certain intellectual faculty, which they had abused to defile even the holy things of the Word and of doctrine.
Under Defile, see these references. AE 195:3.
They would thus defile the Divine. AC 7290:end.
If there is one falsity... the truths themselves remaining are thus defiled...
The lowest and natural things are more defiled with evils and falsities than interior ones...
The sanctuaries... were defiled when the people sinned.
The good which flows in he defiles with merit.
Hence the Divine cannot flow in, because the instant it does so, it is immersed in thoughts about self, and is defiled.
All the defilement of man is effected through falsities opposed to the truths of wisdom.
The love or will is defiled in the understanding, and by it, if they are not elevated together. General article.
Love denied in the understanding, and by it, becomes natural, sensuous, and corporeal. General article.
Under Defile, see these references. AR 620. DLW 419.
The Roman Catholic religiosity... has defiled and profaned the things of the Word and of the Church. Signified.
